title: Papillary Tumour of the Pineal Region, in a Child With a Germline PTEN Pathogenic Variant, Arisen in the Fourth Ventricle
summary: A 2-year-old boy with a germline PTEN variant had a tumour in the fourth ventricle, with no connection to the pineal region, whose methylation profile matched PTPR-B with loss of chromosome 10.
adds: Suggests PTPR can arise outside the pineal region and strengthens the PTEN link.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region Presenting With Obstructive Hydrocephalus: A Diagnostic and Management Challenge
summary: A 45-year-old woman needed review at two neuropathology centres before PTPR was confirmed. Her ETV failed and she required a shunt; after resection and radiotherapy there was no recurrence on latest imaging.
adds: Highlights diagnostic difficulty and the need for permanent CSF diversion when ETV fails.

title: Combined Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy and Biopsy of Rare Pineal Region Tumor Using Single Burr Hole Approach
summary: A 42-year-old man had combined ETV and biopsy through a single burr hole. The ETV later failed and a shunt was needed, after which he was discharged well.
adds: Describes a minimally invasive way to diagnose PTPR and treat hydrocephalus at once.

title: Fractionated Gamma Knife Radiation for Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: A Case Report and Literature Review
summary: A 24-year-old man with a recurrent grade 3 tumour that had progressed after partial removal and radiotherapy was treated with a second partial removal and fractionated Gamma Knife (28 Gy in 8 sessions). The tumour shrank markedly and he was stable at one year.
adds: First report of fractionated Gamma Knife as salvage for a large recurrent PTPR.

title: Papillary Tumor of Pineal Region; A Case Report
journal: Middle Eastern Cancer and Oncology Journal
summary: A 4-year-old boy with hydrocephalus had a shunt, complete tumour removal and then radiotherapy to the tumour bed. Six months later there was no recurrence and no neurological deficit. The authors stress careful radiotherapy planning in young children to protect brain development.
adds: Adds a rare preschool-age case treated with surgery plus adjuvant radiotherapy.

title: Case Report: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region (PTRP)
journal: Journal of Neurological Surgery Part B: Skull Base
summary: Follows a 29-year-old man over about eight years: complete removal in 2016, recurrence at four years treated with radiotherapy, further growth two years later requiring re-operation. The authors conclude that lifelong neurological follow-up is essential.
adds: A long individual timeline showing recurrence even after apparently complete removal.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region Treated With Surgery and Postoperative Radiotherapy: A Case Report
summary: A man in his late 60s presented with confusion and unsteadiness from hydrocephalus. He was treated with surgery and radiotherapy and was symptom-free with no recurrence at 18 months. The paper reviews prognostic features and gives radiotherapy planning volumes.
adds: A Canadian case with practical detail on how adjuvant radiotherapy is planned.

title: Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region (PTPR) in Pediatric Population: A Case Report and Literature Review
summary: Reports a 3-year-old whose tumour stayed stable for over nine years after partial removal and radiotherapy, and reviews 35 published paediatric cases. Recurrence occurred in about 39% after complete removal and 60% after partial removal; radiotherapy seemed to help after incomplete surgery.
adds: The largest review of childhood PTPR to date, quantifying recurrence by extent of surgery.

title: Two illustrative cases of papillary tumor of the pineal region: Clinical presentation, management, and outcomes
summary: Two women (47 and 40) both presented with hydrocephalus symptoms and had biopsy, ventriculostomy, surgery and radiotherapy. One achieved long-lasting control; the other developed aggressive metastatic disease despite repeated treatment.
adds: Shows how differently PTPR can behave in two similarly treated patients.

title: Occipital Transtentorial Approach for Resection of Papillary Tumor of Pineal Region: Two-Dimensional Operative Video
journal: Journal of Neurological Surgery Part B: Skull Base
summary: An operative video of a 46-year-old man with a grade 2 PTPR removed through a right occipital transtentorial approach, explaining the anatomical landmarks used.
adds: Teaching material on one surgical route to the pineal region.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region Identified by DNA Methylation Leads to the Incidental Finding of Germline Mutation PTEN G132D Associated with PTEN Hamartoma Tumor Syndrome: A Case Report and Systematic Review
summary: A 21-year-old man's tumour, first misdiagnosed as ependymoma, was reclassified as PTPR group B by methylation profiling. Sequencing found a PTEN mutation that proved to be inherited (PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome). The systematic review found inconsistent diagnostics and under-use of molecular testing.
adds: First link between PTPR and inherited PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
summary: Nineteen patients from six centres had stereotactic radiosurgery (as primary, adjuvant or salvage treatment). Local control was achieved initially in all, with median progression-free survival of five years; six recurred and were mostly re-treated. Estimated survival was 83% at ten years and 69% at twenty.
adds: The largest radiosurgery series, supporting SRS as a safe primary or adjuvant option.

title: Adjuvant radiotherapy for papillary tumor of the pineal region: a case report with a narrative review of the literature
summary: A 24-year-old woman received radiotherapy (59.4 Gy) after partial removal. Two years later she was well with no recurrence and a slightly smaller residual tumour.
adds: Supports modern high-dose adjuvant radiotherapy after incomplete removal.

title: Constitutional variants in PTEN: a frequent finding in patients with papillary tumors of the pineal region subtype B (PTPR-B) associated with isolated loss of chromosome 10
summary: Reports that inherited (constitutional) PTEN variants are a frequent finding in patients with PTPR subtype B whose tumours show isolated loss of chromosome 10.
adds: Suggests genetic counselling and germline PTEN testing for selected PTPR-B patients.

title: EPCO-28. THE MOLECULAR LANDSCAPE AND ITS PROGNOSTIC IMPLICATIONS IN ADULT PAPILLARY TUMORS OF THE PINEAL REGION - A MULTICENTER YOUNGNOA INVESTIGATION
summary: Methylation and copy-number analysis of 64 adult PTPRs confirmed the A and B subtypes and found that tumours with shorter progression-free survival had hypermethylation of GPCR signalling genes and signs of accelerated epigenetic ageing.
adds: Points to new prognostic markers beyond the A/B subtype split.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region with Leptomeningeal Seeding: A Case Report and Literature Review
summary: A 46-year-old man had surgery and radiotherapy, but 14 months later the tumour had spread along the brain and spinal coverings. Chemotherapy with vincristine and carboplatin halted progression for at least six months.
adds: Shows that chemotherapy can stabilise PTPR that has spread through the cerebrospinal fluid.

title: Papillary Tumours of Pineal Region: A single centre experience in management of 11 cases
summary: A single centre reviewed 11 patients (average age 33). Eight had complete removal, four received chemoradiotherapy, and none of the nine with follow-up (average 45 months) recurred. Extent of removal appeared to be the main determinant of prognosis.
adds: One of the larger single-centre surgical series, with no recurrences at medium-term follow-up.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Gland: Series of Four Clinical Cases
summary: Four patients presented with hydrocephalus symptoms such as headache, seizures, visual and gait problems and Parinaud syndrome; all had surgery and the diagnosis was confirmed by pathology.
adds: Adds a Mexican series of four cases.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: analysis of DNA methylation profiles and clinical outcomes in 76 cases
summary: Combined 39 new and 37 published cases, all confirmed by DNA methylation, into a cohort of 76. The authors refined the known subtypes into PTPR-A, PTPR-B1 and PTPR-B2; nearly half of patients with follow-up had progression, and the rate differed between subtypes.
adds: The largest molecular cohort so far, proposing three methylation subtypes with differing progression risk.

title: Determination of Optimal Treatment Plan for Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Case Series With Literature Review
summary: Combined three new cases with 105 from the literature. Survival was 97% at one year, 88% at five and 80% at ten; progression-free survival was 57%. Surgery followed by stereotactic radiosurgery had the best progression-free survival, and surgery with chemotherapy plus radiotherapy the best ten-year survival.
adds: Proposes surgery plus radiosurgery as a preferred strategy based on pooled data.

title: DNA methylation profiling in a case of papillary tumor of the pineal region
journal: Journal of Neuropathology and Experimental Neurology
summary: A 52-year-old woman had ETV and biopsy. DNA methylation profiling confirmed PTPR and placed it in the less aggressive subtype A, which led the team to monitor rather than operate aggressively.
adds: Illustrates how methylation subtyping can directly change a treatment decision.

title: SNO-EANO-EURACAN consensus on management of pineal parenchymal tumors
summary: An international consensus (SNO-EANO-EURACAN) giving pragmatic recommendations for managing pineal parenchymal tumours and PTPR, incorporating the molecular groupings in the 2021 WHO classification.
adds: The current expert consensus on PTPR management.

title: Papillary Tumor of Pineal Region: A Case Report
summary: A short report of a 27-year-old woman whose pineal tumour was removed and proved to be PTPR on microscopy and immunostaining. It reviews how PTPR fits among pineal region tumours.
adds: Adds a case from Bangladesh to the world literature.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: A Case Report and Literature Review
journal: American Journal of Clinical and Experimental Medicine
summary: A case report and literature review noting that PTPR has few specific clinical features, so a definite diagnosis before surgery is usually not possible.
adds: Reiterates the difficulty of pre-operative diagnosis.

title: An Unusual Finding: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region
summary: A 61-year-old woman presented with hydrocephalus symptoms. The report walks through imaging, surgery and pathology, and notes a recurrence rate around 56% in the literature.
adds: Adds an older-adult case from the United States.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region in pediatric patient – A case report
summary: A 9-year-old girl presented unusually with months of excessive appetite and weight gain. Complete removal plus local radiotherapy was followed by 78 months without recurrence.
adds: A paediatric case with an unusual presentation and long recurrence-free follow-up.

title: OTHR-15. Papillary tumor of the pineal region: case series of this rare pediatric entity
summary: Three children (22 months, 8 years and 7 years) were treated with partial or complete removal, with radiotherapy in one. All remained free of progression at 8 to 92 months. Genetic testing found no targetable mutations.
adds: Suggests that some children do well even after partial removal without adjuvant therapy.

title: NCOG-34. METASTATIC PAPILLARY TUMOR OF THE PINEAL REGION: ROLE OF STEREOTACTIC IRRADIATION AND ADJUVANT TEMOZOLOMIDE
summary: A 41-year-old man had recurrence in the cerebellar coverings treated with craniospinal proton therapy, then a new deposit inside the temporal lobe treated with surgery, Gamma Knife and temozolomide. He was well 21 months later.
adds: First description of PTPR spreading into brain tissue away from the pineal region, and a successful salvage strategy.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region Rare Pediatric CNS Tumor Case Series Treated in King Fahad Medical City (KFMC)
summary: Three girls treated in Riyadh, with diagnosis confirmed by DNA methylation. One with spinal spread was controlled by radiotherapy alone; one with repeated local regrowth responded to intensive chemotherapy; one recurred after 18 months and was salvaged by re-operation and focal radiotherapy.
adds: Shows responses to three different treatment strategies in children, including chemotherapy.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Pineal Region Tumors in Adults: A EURACAN Overview
summary: A European expert overview of adult pineal region tumours, including PTPR, covering imaging, surgery, radiotherapy and systemic treatment. For PTPR and similar tumours, radiotherapy is usually reserved for grade 3 or recurrent disease.
adds: Places PTPR within current European (EURACAN) management recommendations.

title: High Myoinositol on Proton MR Spectroscopy Could Be a Potential Signature of Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region—Case Report of Two Patients
summary: In two confirmed cases, pre-surgical MR spectroscopy showed extremely high myo-inositol, a pattern very different from other pineal tumours, possibly reflecting the tumour's ependymal nature.
adds: Proposes a non-invasive spectroscopy signature to suspect PTPR before surgery.

title: P14.89 Papillary tumor of the pineal region: three cases from a single institution
summary: Three adults treated in Buenos Aires had biopsy, surgery and chemoradiotherapy with temozolomide. One had a distant recurrence after seven years and then remained stable; the other two were recurrence-free at 2 to 2.5 years.
adds: First series from Argentina; supports aggressive multimodal treatment.

title: Papillary Tumor of Pineal Region in a 5-Year-Old Male Child: A Rare Entity
summary: A 5-year-old boy with headaches, a large head since birth and visual problems had complete removal through an approach beneath the cerebellum. Only six prior cases under 16 were found.
adds: Adds a very young Indian case.

title: Recurrent Papillary Tumor of Pineal Region Misdiagnosed as Pineocytoma 9-Years Ago
summary: A 29-year-old man had a recurrence nine years after a tumour misdiagnosed as pineocytoma. Surgery, shunting and radiotherapy controlled it for eight years before two recurrences within six months with rising proliferation.
adds: A long timeline showing late recurrence and eventual acceleration.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: Is stereotactic radiosurgery efficient for this rare entity?
summary: A 26-year-old woman declined open surgery after biopsy and ETV and was treated with stereotactic radiosurgery instead. At one year her tumour had shrunk by about 60% and she had regained independence.
adds: Supports radiosurgery as a primary option when surgery is refused or risky.

title: [Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region:Report of One Case]
summary: A Chinese case report describing slight high density on CT and bright T1 signal with cystic change and strong enhancement on MRI.
adds: Confirms the typical imaging appearance in a Chinese patient.

title: PTEN R130Q Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region (PTPR) with Chromosome 10 Loss Successfully Treated with Everolimus: A Case Report
summary: A grade 3 PTPR with a PTEN R130Q mutation and chromosome 10 loss recurred after surgery and radiotherapy. Treatment with the mTOR inhibitor everolimus alone led to tumour regression and a long symptom-free period.
adds: First targeted drug therapy (everolimus) reported to shrink PTPR.

title: Pineal Parenchymal Tumor of Intermediate Differentiation (PPTID) and Papillary Tumor of Pineal Region (PTPR): A Review
summary: Reviewed 45 PTPR and 25 PPTID articles to contrast the two entities. Surgery improved survival in both; radiotherapy clearly helped PPTID but showed little effect in PTPR, and chemotherapy was not shown to help either.
adds: Clarifies differences between PTPR and the often-confused PPTID.

title: Papillary tumour of the pineal region: a case report
journal: Egyptian Journal of Neurology, Psychiatry and Neurosurgery
summary: Reports a 24-year-old man who presented unusually with seizures and reduced consciousness from a large solid-cystic pineal tumour. The paper discusses how PTPR can be mistaken for ependymoma or choroid plexus papilloma, and argues for early aggressive treatment because of the risk of spread.
adds: Adds an African case with an atypical seizure presentation and a poor outcome.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region with Parinaud Syndrome: A Case Report
summary: A 17-year-old girl with Parinaud syndrome had a large solid-cystic mass that was bright on T1 MRI and dense on CT. The authors propose that this combination should raise suspicion of PTPR.
adds: Describes CT and MRI clues that can suggest PTPR before surgery.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region in pediatric populations: An additional case and systematic review of a rare tumor entity
summary: A 10-year-old girl with trisomy 21 was treated with CSF diversion and complete removal and was recurrence-free at three years. The authors systematically reviewed paediatric cases and caution against simply applying adult protocols to children.
adds: First PTPR reported with Down syndrome, plus a paediatric systematic review.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: a single-center experience
summary: A German centre reviews its experience, noting diverse presentations, the challenge of timely diagnosis, and recent advances in immunostaining, molecular testing and surgery.
adds: Single-centre perspective on modern diagnosis and management.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: A Case with Unique Immunohistochemical Keratin Expression Pattern
journal: Indian Journal of Medical and Paediatric Oncology
summary: A 25-year-old man's tumour showed an unusual membranous and dot-like keratin staining pattern on immunohistochemistry and electron microscopy.
adds: Expands the range of staining patterns pathologists may encounter.

title: Increased VEGF levels in a case of papillary tumor of the pineal region with intracranial hemorrhage: a potential surrogate indicator of tumor angiogenesis and aggressiveness?
summary: A 40-year-old man presented unconscious from bleeding into the tumour. Blood VEGF levels were very high and fell after radiotherapy shrank the tumour, suggesting VEGF as a possible marker of tumour activity.
adds: Rare haemorrhagic presentation and a proposed blood marker.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: Case report and review of the literature
summary: Describes a 34-year-old man whose cystic pineal tumour, thought on scans to be a pineocytoma, was completely removed through an approach beneath the cerebellum. He had no further treatment and stayed free of recurrence for almost five years. The authors also gathered every published case treated by complete removal alone.
adds: Evidence that complete removal without radiotherapy can give long recurrence-free survival in selected patients.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Systematic Review and Analysis of Prognostic Factors
summary: A systematic review of 177 patients from 71 publications (mean age 33). About 57% recurred after a median of 29 months; survival at three years was 83.5%. Larger tumour size predicted worse survival and having surgery predicted better survival, but no benefit of complete removal or adjuvant therapy was detected.
adds: The largest patient-level analysis of outcomes and prognostic factors.

title: PAPILLARY TUMOUR OF PINEAL REGION- A RARE CASE REPORT
journal: Journal of Evolution of Medical and Dental Sciences
summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with failing vision, incontinence and confusion; scans showed a 3 cm pineal mass with hydrocephalus.
adds: Adds an Indian case with an advanced presentation.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region in an Adolescent
journal: Indian Journal of Medical and Paediatric Oncology
summary: A letter reporting PTPR in a 15-year-old, noting fewer than 100 cases published at the time.
adds: Adds an adolescent Indian case.

title: Radiotherapy for papillary tumor of the pineal region: A systematic review of the literature
summary: A systematic review of radiotherapy in PTPR: 72% of reported patients received it, at widely varying doses. Toxicity was low and ten-year survival about 72%, but local recurrence reached about 60% at five years and over 80% at ten.
adds: Summarises radiotherapy practice and outcomes and calls for prospective studies.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Case Report and Literature Review
summary: A 36-year-old woman with a year of headache and double vision needed an emergency shunt, then partial tumour removal. She did well but a local recurrence appeared 3.5 years later and was treated with radiotherapy. The review stresses that most patients present with raised pressure and that local recurrence is common.
adds: Illustrates late local recurrence after partial removal and the typical presentation.

title: Recurrent Pineocytomalike Papillary Tumor of The Pineal Region: A Case Report and Literature Review
summary: A 28-year-old man was diagnosed with pineocytoma and had complete removal; seven years later the tumour recurred and cytokeratin staining revealed it was PTPR. Radiotherapy produced marked shrinkage.
adds: Warns that PTPR can mimic benign pineocytoma unless cytokeratin staining is done.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: A Case Report
summary: A 6-year-old boy was treated after biopsy with radiotherapy (54 Gy) and chemotherapy rather than removal. The tumour shrank slightly and he was well and at school four years later.
adds: Supports radical radiotherapy as a main treatment option when surgery is not pursued.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region in Children: Presentation of a Case and Comprehensive Literature Review
summary: A 3-year-old boy with a recurrent tumour had complete removal, radiotherapy and chemotherapy and was recurrence-free over three years later. The tumour had progressed from grade 2 to grade 3. The paper reviews the 19 childhood cases then published.
adds: Documents malignant progression at recurrence and reviews paediatric management.

title: A case of rare Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region (PTPR) with leptomeningeal metastases treated with Bevacizumab and Chemotherapy (P6.135)
summary: A 46-year-old man had repeated radiosurgery over years, then spread to the brain and spine. After temozolomide, he was treated with bevacizumab plus etoposide and later carboplatin, achieving stable disease for about a year.
adds: Suggests bevacizumab-based chemotherapy for heavily pre-treated, disseminated PTPR.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region
summary: A 21-year-old woman had complete removal through a supracerebellar infratentorial approach. The authors discuss surgical approach and recommend adjuvant treatment because recurrence rates are high.
adds: Adds a Turkish case with surgical detail.

title: The Role of Adjuvant Radiotherapy in the Treatment of Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region: Some General Considerations and a Case Report
summary: A 27-year-old woman who had several operations received conformal radiotherapy (59.4 Gy) to the residual tumour. At 41 months she had a complete response, no side effects and resolution of symptoms.
adds: Supports a role for higher-dose adjuvant radiotherapy.

title: Papillary tumor of pineal region: Case reports
journal: Journal of Medical and Scientific Research
summary: Two patients with headache and eye-movement problems were initially thought to have ependymoma on rapid intra-operative smears. Both tumours recurred within a year of surgery.
adds: Highlights the diagnostic pitfalls and early recurrence after surgery alone.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Clinical Presentations, Prognostic Factors, Treatments, and Outcomes
summary: A pooled analysis of 73 published patients (mean age 33.5). Headache was the commonest symptom (80%). Fifty had no recurrence at reporting and three had died; median disease-free survival was 24 months, with 50% disease-free at five years and 25% at ten.
adds: Quantified recurrence patterns and showed that aggressive spread, though uncommon, does occur.

title: Long-term follow-up of a papillary tumor of the pineal region: addendum to a case report
summary: An addendum providing long-term follow-up of the Siena patient first reported by Cerase and colleagues in 2009.
adds: Extends the follow-up of one of the best-documented natural-history cases.

title: Papillary tumor of pineal region: A rare entity
summary: A 60-year-old woman presented with headache, giddiness and reduced vision two years after a previous pineal tumour operation; imaging showed a haemorrhagic recurrence.
adds: Adds a recurrent case in an older patient.

title: Cytologic features of papillary tumor of the pineal region: A case report showing tigroid background
summary: Describes the appearance of PTPR on rapid intra-operative smears from a 34-year-old woman, including true papillary fragments and a lace-like background usually associated with germinoma.
adds: Helps pathologists recognise PTPR during surgery and avoid confusing it with germinoma.

title: Late dissemination via cerebrospinal fluid of papillary tumor of the pineal region: a case report and literature review
summary: Describes a patient whose tumour spread to the ventricles and spine five years after the original operation, and reviews other reports of CSF spread.
adds: Shows that spread via cerebrospinal fluid can occur years after treatment.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: A Distinct Molecular Entity
summary: Studied 24 PTPRs: all tested showed loss of chromosome 10, and losses of 3 and 22q and gains of 8p and 12 were common. Methylation profiling separated PTPR from ependymoma and PPTID and revealed two groups, one with shorter progression-free survival. The SPDEF protein was a useful marker.
adds: Defined PTPR as a distinct molecular entity and introduced the two methylation groups.

title: A case of papillary tumor of the pineal region with a long clinical history: molecular characterization and therapeutic consideration with review of the literature
summary: A man followed from age 22 to 37 had several diagnoses before PTPR was confirmed, with repeated partial removals, chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Temozolomide plus bevacizumab produced a partial response lasting over 14 months.
adds: First report of temozolomide-bevacizumab response in PTPR.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region-report of three cases with literature review
summary: Three patients with headache and visual disturbance all had surgery and radiotherapy. Followed for 8 months to 8 years, one recurred after seven years while two stayed free of disease.
adds: Adds Indian cases with long follow-up and consistent staining features.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: A case report and review of the literature
summary: A 10-year-old girl had the tumour removed and was recurrence-free at 15 months. The review found only seven previous cases in children under 16.
adds: Adds a paediatric case from China and tallies childhood cases.

title: Papillary tumor of pineal region with an unusual clinical presentation: Case report and review of the literature
summary: A 17-year-old girl's tumour extended into the third ventricle; the paper describes its microscopic and immunostaining features in detail.
adds: Adds an adolescent case with an atypical extent.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region with synchronous suprasellar focus and novel cytogenetic features
summary: A 25-year-old man had two tumours at once, in the pineal and suprasellar regions, with losses of chromosomes 3, 7, 10, 14, 18 and Y. He was stable 17 months after surgery and radiotherapy.
adds: First multicentric PTPR and new chromosome findings.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: Histopathological characterization and review of the literature
summary: The team that first described PTPR summarises its microscopic, immunostaining and electron-microscopy features, the main look-alikes, and the proposed origin from subcommissural organ cells.
adds: Authoritative pathological description from the original describers.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: MR Signal Intensity Correlated to Histopathology
summary: A 17-year-old man with headache had a histologically confirmed PTPR. The authors relate the T1-bright MRI signal to the tumour's pathology and note that this sign, when not explained by fat, calcium, melanin or blood, should suggest PTPR.
adds: Correlates MRI signal with tissue findings.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region with extended clinical and radiologic follow-up
summary: A patient treated with partial removal, Gamma Knife radiosurgery and temozolomide had regression of the residual tumour and remained symptom-free over nine years.
adds: Suggests radiosurgery plus temozolomide can give long-term control after incomplete removal.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region. Report of two cases and literature review
summary: Two patients had complete removal through a supracerebellar infratentorial approach plus radiotherapy. A 37-year-old man was well 10 years after onset; a 45-year-old woman was well at two years.
adds: Supports complete removal as the main prognostic factor.

title: Clinicopathological characteristics of papillary tumor of the pineal region
journal: Chinese Journal of Contemporary Neurology and Neurosurgery
summary: A 57-year-old man had complete removal of a grade 2-3 PTPR and received no radiotherapy or chemotherapy; he had no deficit or recurrence at 12 months. The paper discusses look-alike tumours.
adds: Adds a Chinese case treated with surgery alone.

title: Increased Mitotic and Proliferative Activity Are Associated With Worse Prognosis in Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region
summary: In 21 patients (median age 35), 63% progressed and 16% died. Only increased mitotic activity and a high Ki-67 proliferation index were significantly linked to recurrence.
adds: Identified mitotic and proliferative activity as prognostic markers.

title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery of a Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Case Report and Review of the Literature
summary: The first report of radiosurgery for biopsy-confirmed PTPR: after stereotactic biopsy, Gamma Knife treatment led to continued tumour shrinkage five years later.
adds: Introduced radiosurgery as a treatment option for PTPR.

title: [Clinicopathologic features of papillary tumors of the pineal region]
summary: Among 386 pineal region tumours, five were PTPR. Staining was consistent across cases; three patients were alive and one with recurrence died. The authors found PTPR more common in males.
adds: Chinese pathology series establishing frequency and staining profile.

title: Role of surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy in papillary tumors of the pineal region: a multicenter study
summary: A multicentre series of 44 patients followed for a median of 63 months: 32 were alive, 12 progressed and median progression-free survival was 58 months. Only complete removal and younger age were linked to longer survival; radiotherapy and chemotherapy showed no significant effect.
adds: The key multicentre treatment study emphasising complete removal.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region with anaplastic small cell component
summary: A 59-year-old woman's PTPR contained an anaplastic small-cell component with very high proliferation. It regrew within two months of surgery and responded to single-session robotic radiosurgery.
adds: First PTPR with an anaplastic component, showing malignant potential.

title: Four-year clinical and neuroradiological follow-up of a papillary tumor of the pineal region
summary: A 47-year-old man was followed with CT and MRI for about four years before surgery, allowing the tumour's growth rate to be measured. The authors advocate early surgery once PTPR is suspected.
adds: Provides a measured growth rate for an untreated PTPR.

title: Complete regression of papillary tumor of the pineal region after radiation therapy: case report and review of the literature
summary: A 23-year-old man had ETV and endoscopic biopsy only, then radiotherapy, which made the tumour disappear completely with no recurrence at 25 months.
adds: Shows that biopsy plus radiotherapy can be an alternative to open surgery.

title: 45 YEAR OLD MAN WITH A PINEAL REGION TUMOR FOR OVER 15 YEARS
summary: A 45-year-old man managed with a shunt was observed for 15 years as his tumour slowly grew, then had near-total removal confirming PTPR.
adds: Documents extremely slow growth over 15 years.

title: Cellular pleomorphism in papillary tumors of the pineal region
summary: Two men (48 and 35) had tumours with varying degrees of cell pleomorphism. Pleomorphic areas showed low proliferation, suggesting a degenerative rather than aggressive change.
adds: Helps pathologists avoid over-grading pleomorphic PTPR.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Ultrastructural Study of a Case
summary: An in-depth electron-microscopy study of one case confirming combined ependymal, neuroendocrine and secretory features, with some differences from earlier descriptions.
adds: Detailed ultrastructural evidence for the ependymal origin of PTPR.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region: Diagnosis and Treatment
summary: An overview of PTPR covering its origin, imaging (notably T1 brightness), high local recurrence (up to 70%), rare spinal spread (up to 7%) and treatment with surgery followed by radiotherapy.
adds: Compact reference summary of diagnosis and treatment.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: two case studies and a review of the literature
journal: Annals of Clinical and Laboratory Science
summary: Two patients seen within three months prompted a review of 59 reported cases (ages 5 to 66, mean 32). The paper summarises typical presentation, imaging (often resembling pineocytoma) and the staining pattern that separates PTPR from ependymoma.
adds: An early consolidated review of the first ~60 cases.

title: Papillary tumour of the pineal region
summary: A 25-year-old woman and a 42-year-old man both had surgery and radiotherapy; one had a local recurrence at 23 months. The paper reviews the emerging consistent features of this then-new entity.
adds: Adds Australian cases and summarises early literature.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region in a 15-month-old boy
summary: A 15-month-old boy, the youngest reported, was initially thought to have a tectal glioma. The tumour grew despite debulking and chemotherapy and he needed multiple hydrocephalus procedures; after proton therapy it was stable at 15 months.
adds: Extended the known age range of PTPR to infancy.

title: Papillary tumor of pineal region: report of three cases and review of literature
summary: Three patients showed characteristic imaging and uniform microscopic features without aggressive histology. Only 55 cases had been reported at the time.
adds: Adds Indian cases and calls for multicentre study.

title: Papillary tumor of pineal region presenting with leptomeningeal seeding
summary: A 39-year-old woman had PTPR that had already seeded the pituitary stalk and inner-ear canals at diagnosis. Radiosurgery shrank the deposits but new ones appeared nearby. The tumour expressed c-Kit.
adds: Proved that PTPR can disseminate to distant sites.

title: Pineal parenchymal tumor of intermediate differentiation with papillary features: a continuum of primary pineal tumors?
summary: A 29-year-old woman's tumour showed features of a pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation transitioning into PTPR, suggesting pineal tumours may form a continuum.
adds: Raised the possibility of overlap between PTPR and other pineal tumours.

title: Natural history of papillary tumor of the pineal region: new insights on biological explanation
summary: A 29-year-old man's tumour, first called ependymoma, grew aggressively within eight months of partial removal. He improved on chemotherapy and radiotherapy. The authors argue that PTPR's variable growth reflects a wide spectrum of differentiation.
adds: A short natural-history example contrasting with slow-growing cases.

title: Advanced magnetic resonance imaging with histopathological correlation in papillary tumor of pineal region: report of a case and review of literature
summary: Advanced MRI in an 18-year-old girl showed T1 brightness, mild diffusion restriction, very high blood volume and flow, and a myo-inositol peak on spectroscopy.
adds: Describes perfusion and spectroscopy features that may relate to recurrence risk.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region
summary: A review describing PTPR as a newly recognised tumour that affects children and adults, is often bright on T1 MRI, and must be distinguished from pineal, choroid plexus, ependymal and meningeal tumours. It recommends careful surgery followed by radiotherapy because of the high local recurrence risk.
adds: An early accessible overview of diagnosis and treatment.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region--a recently described entity: a report of three cases and review of the literature
summary: Three cases diagnosed over four years showed uniform microscopic features with strong staining for synaptophysin, NSE, chromogranin, S-100, MAP-2 and cytokeratin. One was misread on imaging as a tectal glioma.
adds: Adds three Indian cases and notes a radiological pitfall.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: report of a rapidly progressive tumor with possible multicentric origin
summary: A boy's tumour spread early through the cerebrospinal fluid and progressed relentlessly despite intensive chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and he died. Imaging suggested a multicentric origin and intense uptake on octreotide scanning.
adds: Documents the most aggressive end of the PTPR spectrum.

title: Neuroradiological follow-up of the growth of papillary tumor of the pineal region: a case report
summary: A 56-year-old man's tumour was observed on MRI for 29 months and clearly enlarged, then was removed and irradiated. The report documents the natural growth and imaging features.
adds: Rare documentation of untreated PTPR growth over time.

title: Papillary tumour of the pineal region: diagnosis by cytology smear
summary: Describes the distinctive features of PTPR on intra-operative smear preparations and matches them to the tissue biopsy.
adds: Helps rapid intra-operative recognition of PTPR.

title: Clinicopathological features from long-term observation of a papillary tumor of the pineal region (PTPR): a case report
summary: A 17-year-old man's incompletely removed tumour, first called papillary ependymoma, recurred three times; staining later confirmed PTPR. He survived 218 months, the longest reported at the time.
adds: Demonstrates very long survival despite repeated recurrence.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region: a case report
summary: A 43-year-old man had complete removal followed by radiotherapy and chemotherapy and was recurrence-free at one year. Advanced imaging (MR spectroscopy, PET) and a high proliferation index suggested the tumour was biologically active.
adds: Early Japanese case linking imaging and proliferation markers to the argument for adjuvant therapy.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region
summary: A 22-year-old man with headache, nystagmus and double vision had his tumour removed. The report details the mix of epithelial, ependymal and neuroendocrine features and reviews the differential diagnosis.
adds: Detailed pathological description supporting an indolent tumour with tendency to local recurrence.

title: MR Imaging of Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region
summary: Imaging of four patients showed that PTPR is intrinsically bright on T1-weighted MRI and sits in the posterior commissure or pineal region. The authors propose a pathological explanation for this signal.
adds: Defined the key MRI sign (T1 hyperintensity) used to suspect PTPR.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region in a child: case report and review of the literature
summary: A 13-year-old boy had ETV, biopsy, complete removal and radiotherapy (50 Gy). He was back at school with no residual tumour 15 months later.
adds: Early paediatric case arguing for surgery combined with radiotherapy.

title: Papillary tumour of the pineal region
summary: A single patient followed with serial imaging over seven years, illustrating the variable clinical course. The authors recommend complete removal with focal radiotherapy and surveillance of the whole brain and spine.
adds: Long imaging follow-up and a call for whole-CNS surveillance.

title: PAPILLARY TUMORS OF THE PINEAL REGION: CASE REPORT
summary: Three women aged 37 to 55 were initially thought to have cancer that had spread to the pineal region. On review the tumours met the criteria for PTPR. All had near-total removal and radiotherapy; two followed for about five years remained stable.
adds: Showed that some tumours previously labelled metastatic carcinoma were actually PTPR.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region
summary: A 48-year-old woman with a month of morning headaches had complete removal through an occipital transtentorial approach and was recurrence-free at eight months.
adds: Early Japanese case; notes PTPR may previously have been mislabelled as ependymoma or choroid plexus papilloma.

title: Prognosis and Histopathologic Features in Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region: A Retrospective Multicenter Study of 31 Cases
journal: Journal of Neuropathology and Experimental Neurology
summary: A multicentre series of 31 patients (ages 5 to 66, median 29). Complete removal was achieved in 21 and 15 received radiotherapy, yet most recurred: five-year overall survival was 73% and progression-free survival only 27%.
adds: First sizeable outcome series; established that local recurrence is the rule.

title: Papillary tumor of the pineal region--a new pathological entity
summary: The third publication on PTPR: a young woman with raised pressure and Parinaud syndrome had her tumour removed. The report describes microscopic, immunostaining and electron-microscopy features.
adds: Early confirmation of PTPR as a reproducible entity.

title: Papillary neuroepithelial tumor of the pineal region. A case report
summary: One of the first reports after PTPR was described: a 29-year-old woman with headaches and hydrocephalus. Detailed staining showed the tumour produced transthyretin, supporting an origin from the subcommissural organ.
adds: Early supporting evidence for the subcommissural-organ origin of PTPR.

title: Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region
summary: The paper that first defined PTPR, describing six patients (four women, two men, aged 19 to 53) with a uniform papillary tumour showing strong cytokeratin staining. The features resembled the ependymal cells of the subcommissural organ, proposed as the cell of origin.
adds: Established PTPR as a distinct tumour entity.
